title: Padding oracle programs

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; section 15.1, Exercise 15.3, pp.63–64; the specified oracle syntax, finite avoidance and injective halting recodings are expanded explicitly

summary: Construct one injective padding map for all oracles and sharpen relative halting completeness to ordinary injective reductions.
abstract: A program allowed to ask membership questions can have infinitely many different codes with exactly the same behavior. We construct these new codes by inserting a numerical tag and discarding it before the old program runs. The translation is an ordinary algorithm: it never asks the oracle used by the program it produces. Its injectivity lets a bounded search avoid any finite list of forbidden names. The same syntax argument shows that freezing an old input into a new program retains that input injectively. As a result, every membership problem recognizable with an oracle translates injectively into that oracle's diagonal halting problem. Two fixed injective translations also relate diagonal halting to halting on input zero, simultaneously for all oracles.
